flags: Central contributed its pet distribution business to a new partnership with Phillips Pet Food & Supplies. It received cash proceeds of approximately $31 million and a 20% ownership interest, and recognized a pre-tax gain of $2.5 million. The business had fiscal 2025 net sales of $474 million.

Central signed a Sale and Purchase Agreement to acquire about 80% of TRIXIE for total consideration of up to €400 million, including an upfront €340 million in cash. Closing is subject to regulatory approval.
In its Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings release, Central raised its fiscal 2026 outlook for non-GAAP diluted EPS from $2.70 or better to $2.85 or better. This is a guidance raise, not a withdrawal.

business_model.claim: The company reports two segments, Pet and Garden.
quotes: We operate through two reportable segments: Pet and Garden.

business_model.claim: The Pet segment sells dog and cat supplies such as treats, chews, toys, beds, grooming items and waste management products. It also sells aquatics, small animal, reptile, bird, equine, animal health and insect control products, live fish and small animals, and outdoor cushions.
quotes: Our Pet segment offers a broad range of products for dog and cat supplies, including treats and chews, toys, beds and containment, grooming items, waste management and training pads.

business_model.claim: The Garden segment sells lawn and garden consumables: grass seed, packet seed, wild bird feed, herbicides and pesticides, fertilizers and live plants.
quotes: Our Garden segment includes lawn and garden consumables such as grass seed; vegetable, flower and herb packet seed; wild bird feed, bird houses and other birding accessories; weed, grass, and other herbicides, insecticide and pesticide products; fertilizers and live plants.

business_model.claim: In fiscal 2025, net sales were $3.1 billion. Pet contributed approximately $1.8 billion and Garden approximately $1.3 billion.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, our consolidated net sales were $3.1 billion, of which our Pet segment, or Pet, accounted for approximately $1.8 billion and our Garden segment, or Garden, accounted for approximately $1.3 billion.

business_model.claim: Fiscal 2025 operating income was $250 million. It was made up of Pet income of $216 million and Garden income of $142 million, less corporate expenses of $108 million.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, our operating income was $250 million, consisting of income from our Pet segment of $216 million, income from our Garden segment of $142 million and corporate expenses of $108 million.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from three sources: the company's own brands, private label products made for retailers, and distribution of third-party brands. Branded products were approximately 79% of fiscal 2025 net sales and other manufacturers' products were 21%.
quotes: We produce both branded and private label products for our customers as well as distribute third-party brands that give our retail partners a breadth of selection from ultra-premium to value offerings.

business_model.claim: The company sells mainly to retailers, both brick-and-mortar and online.
quotes: We have long-standing relationships with leading national, regional and independent retailers across brick-and-mortar and online channels.

business_model.claim: Sales are concentrated in a few retailers. Walmart was approximately 17% and Home Depot approximately 16% of fiscal 2025 net sales. Walmart, Home Depot, Costco, Lowe's and Amazon together were approximately 54%.
quotes: Walmart, our largest customer, accounted for approximately 17% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 16% in fiscal 2024.
Home Depot, our second largest customer, represented approximately 16% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 17% in fiscal 2024.

business_model.claim: Concentrated retailers put pressure on the company's pricing.
quotes: They are more capable of resisting price increases and can demand lower pricing.

business_model.claim: Garden sales are highly seasonal. In fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of Garden net sales and 57% of total net sales fell in the second and third fiscal quarters.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of our Garden segment’s net sales and 57% of our total net sales occurred during our second and third fiscal quarters.

business_model.claim: Weather is a driver of Garden revenue. Cool, wet weather early in the season reduced fiscal 2025 sales in controls and live plants.
quotes: Because demand for lawn and garden products is significantly influenced by weather, particularly weekend weather during the peak gardening season, our results of operations and cash flow could also be adversely affected by certain weather patterns such as unseasonably cool or warm temperatures, heavy rains, water shortages or floods.

business_model.basis: stated in P3; balances from F1
business_model.claim: Seasonal selling ties up working capital. Industry practice is to give retailers extended credit terms or promotional discounts to stock up ahead of the season.
quotes: To encourage retailers and distributors to stock large quantities of inventory, industry practice has been for manufacturers to give extended credit terms and/or promotional discounts.

business_model.claim: Commodity seed and grain prices are a cost driver for bird feed and grass seed. Low grass seed prices led to a write-down of approximately $20 million in fiscal 2024.
quotes: In particular, our Pennington and Kaytee businesses are exposed to fluctuations in market prices for commodity seeds and grains used to produce bird feed and grass seed.

business_model.claim: Tariffs affect costs. Less than 15% of fiscal 2025 cost of goods sold came from outside the United States, mainly from China, Brazil and Mexico.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, less than 15% of our cost of goods sold was from products or materials sourced from outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil and Mexico.

business_model.claim: The Cost and Simplicity program, which consolidates plants and streamlines products, helped lift fiscal 2025 gross margin to 31.9% from 29.5%.
quotes: Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 31.9% in fiscal 2025 from 29.5% in fiscal 2024.

business_model.claim: In April 2026 the company contributed its lower-margin pet distribution business to a partnership with Phillips. It received cash, a note and a 20% ownership interest.
